Those writes cannot be safely unwound, so the affected `APK` value now refuses further installs and record writes with `ErrInstallAborted` rather than producing records built from a stale view. ### Upstream context apk-tools addressed the entry-name half of this class in commit [`c1594f60`](https://gitlab.alpinelinux.org/alpine/apk-tools/-/commit/c1594f60770483625891541375a074fe07338401) (2021-02-04), 'db: consider control characters in filename as malicious', reported by Luca Weiss, with the rationale that 'especially a newline can produce havoc in the database file as the filename is written there as-is'. It added a `contains_control_character()` check rejecting any byte below `0x20` or equal to `0x7f`. It shipped in apk-tools v2.12.2 and, as far as we can determine, was never assigned a CVE. apko reimplements apk in Go and did not inherit this hardening. The initial upstream implementation used a signed `char` comparison, which incorrectly rejected all non-ASCII (multi-byte UTF-8) names; corrected three days later in [`ab7b8e3`](https://gitlab.alpinelinux.org/alpine/apk-tools/-/commit/ab7b8e3c995eb5a05ddbaa4546cd16a10da2d836) ('db: fix control character check to use uint8_t', alpine issue #10737). The Go port compares unsigned bytes and carries regression tests pinning that legitimate UTF-8 names remain acceptable. Upstream applies `contains_control_character()` to the archive entry name only — `src/database.c`, one call site, on `ae->name`. apko matches that scope deliberately: link targets are not validated, because they never become an `F:` or `R:` value and so cannot forge a record, and rejecting them would refuse packages that `apk add` installs without complaint. The metadata variant has no upstream analogue, because apk-tools' line-based `.PKGINFO` reader cannot represent it. ### Related Before [#2328](https://github.com/chainguard-dev/apko/pull/2328), an entry name embedding a single-character line also reached an out-of-range slice panic in `ParseInstalled`, making that denial of service reachable from a package rather than only from a corrupt base image. That specific path is closed by #2328. Two adjacent defects found during this work were fixed publicly ahead of this advisory, as neither was reachable from a package: an infinite loop walking to the filesystem root ([#2389](https://github.com/chainguard-dev/apko/pull/2389)) and a silently discarded record for a package with an empty name ([#2390](https://github.com/chainguard-dev/apko/pull/2390)). A reproducer has been shared with maintainers separately.

GHSA-45cw-mp53-rrv6.title: apk-embedded SPDX documents can hide, impersonate, and displace packages in apko image SBOMs
GHSA-45cw-mp53-rrv6.description: ### Impact apko builds the package portion of an image's SPDX SBOM entirely from SPDX documents that the installed apks ship under `/var/lib/db/sbom`. It never checks that a document describes the package that shipped it, and it omits a package without error when that package's document is missing or fails to parse. A crafted apk can therefore: * remove itself from the image SBOM, * appear under another name and version, with a well-formed PURL, and * replace the record of a genuine package, for example reporting a patched version of a vulnerable library. Tools that trust the SBOM act on the false data: SBOM-driven vulnerability scanners, policy engines that evaluate SBOM attestations, and license reports. apko generates the SBOM before the image is signed, so attestations built from it verify cleanly. The image's `/lib/apk/db/installed` still lists the true package set, so scanners that inspect the image filesystem are unaffected. Images built from repositories whose packages carry no embedded SBOM, such as Alpine, receive an SBOM with no apk packages at all, with no attacker involved. ### Affected data paths All in `pkg/sbom/generator/spdx/spdx.go`, the only SBOM generator in apko: 1. [`locateApkSBOM`](https://github.com/chainguard-dev/apko/blob/e3915900849d95b35f1f5b7c7401922505332152/pkg/sbom/generator/spdx/spdx.go#L185-L206) chooses a document by file name alone, trying `<name>-<version>.spdx.json`, then the version without its `-rN` suffix, then `<name>.spdx.json`. It never checks that the installed package owns the file. 2. [`ProcessInternalApkSBOM`](https://github.com/chainguard-dev/apko/blob/e3915900849d95b35f1f5b7c7401922505332152/pkg/sbom/generator/spdx/spdx.go#L214-L224) returns `nil` when no document matches or the document fails to parse. 3. [`ProcessInternalApkSBOM` and `copySBOMElements`](https://github.com/chainguard-dev/apko/blob/e3915900849d95b35f1f5b7c7401922505332152/pkg/sbom/generator/spdx/spdx.go#L226-L331) copy every package the document describes. Nothing compares name, version, SPDX ID, or PURL against the installed package. 4. [`Generate`](https://github.com/chainguard-dev/apko/blob/e3915900849d95b35f1f5b7c7401922505332152/pkg/sbom/generator/spdx/spdx.go#L163-L173) deduplicates packages by SPDX ID and keeps the first. melange assigns predictable IDs, `SPDXRef-Package-<name>-<version>` ([melange `pkg/sbom/package.go:147`](https://github.com/chainguard-dev/melange/blob/d062cf25ce373bf8045d79b9897878ab207d8d36/pkg/sbom/package.go#L147)), so a document processed earlier can displace a genuine record. 5. [Lines 156-160](https://github.com/chainguard-dev/apko/blob/e3915900849d95b35f1f5b7c7401922505332152/pkg/sbom/generator/spdx/spdx.go#L156-L160) are the only place apk packages enter the SBOM. apko never falls back to the installed database. ### Scope * **Packages built by melange cannot replace their own document.** melange runs the build pipelines ([`pkg/build/build.go:671`](https://github.com/chainguard-dev/melange/blob/d062cf25ce373bf8045d79b9897878ab207d8d36/pkg/build/build.go#L671)) and then writes `<name>-<version>.spdx.json`, truncating any existing file ([`build.go:847`](https://github.com/chainguard-dev/melange/blob/d062cf25ce373bf8045d79b9897878ab207d8d36/pkg/build/build.go#L847), [`pkg/build/sbom/spdx/spdx.go:257`](https://github.com/chainguard-dev/melange/blob/d062cf25ce373bf8045d79b9897878ab207d8d36/pkg/build/sbom/spdx/spdx.go#L257)). * **A melange pipeline can add further `*.spdx.json` files** to `var/lib/db/sbom`. melange's `sbom` linter flags only files without that suffix ([`pkg/linter/linters/sbom.go:30`](https://github.com/chainguard-dev/melange/blob/d062cf25ce373bf8045d79b9897878ab207d8d36/pkg/linter/linters/sbom.go#L30)) and warns by default ([`pkg/linter/linter.go:87-90`](https://github.com/chainguard-dev/melange/blob/d062cf25ce373bf8045d79b9897878ab207d8d36/pkg/linter/linter.go#L87-L90)). apko uses such a file for any co-installed package that lacks a correctly named document of its own. * **No package can overwrite another origin's document.** apko refuses to install two packages from different origins that ship the same path with different content ([`pkg/apk/apk/install.go:141-149`](https://github.com/chainguard-dev/apko/blob/e3915900849d95b35f1f5b7c7401922505332152/pkg/apk/apk/install.go#L141-L149)). ### Attack prerequisites The attacker must place a crafted apk in the resolved package set of a build, for example by publishing it to a repository the build trusts. No access to the build host is required. ### Affected versions All releases through 1.4.5. Unchecked ingestion of embedded documents ships in v0.7.0 and later. Keep-first deduplication by SPDX ID, which enables displacement of genuine records, ships in v0.19.3 and later (#1366). ### Proof of concept A table-driven test against `SPDX.Generate` on an in-memory filesystem, confirmed at `e3915900` and `739e7ce`. `Generate` returns `nil` in every case. | Scenario | Installed | Embedded SBOM | apk entries in image SBOM | | -- | -- | -- | -- | | Substitution | `evil-helper 1.0.0-r0` | `evil-helper-1.0.0-r0.spdx.json` describes `openssl 9.9.9-r0`, `pkg:apk/wolfi/openssl@9.9.9-r0` | `openssl 9.9.9-r0` only | | Missing SBOM | `no-sbom 1.0.0-r0` | none | none | | Malformed SBOM | `broken 1.0.0-r0` | `{not json` | none | | Displacement | `aaa 1.0.0-r0`, `openssl 3.0.1-r0` | `aaa`'s document reuses `SPDXRef-Package-openssl-3.0.1-r0` with version `3.5.0-r0` | `openssl 3.5.0-r0`; the genuine `3.0.1-r0` record is dropped | | Name-only fallback | `busybox 1.36.1-r0`, no document of its own | added `busybox.spdx.json` says `9.9.9-r0` | `busybox 9.9.9-r0` | Save as `pkg/sbom/generator/spdx/embedded_sbom_identity_test.go` and run `go test ./pkg/sbom/generator/spdx/ -run TestEmbeddedSBOMIdentity -v`. Each subtest passes while the defect exists. ```go package spdx import ( 'context' 'encoding/json' 'os' 'path/filepath' 'testing' 'chainguard.dev/apko/pkg/apk/apk' apkfs 'chainguard.dev/apko/pkg/apk/fs' ) func installedPkg(name, version, origin string) *apk.InstalledPackage { return &apk.InstalledPackage{Package: apk.Package{Name: name, Version: version, Origin: origin, Arch: 'x86_64'}} } func embeddedSBOM(id, name, version, purl string) []byte { doc := map[string]any{ 'SPDXID': 'SPDXRef-DOCUMENT', 'spdxVersion': 'SPDX-2.3', 'documentDescribes': []string{id}, 'packages': []map[string]any{{ 'SPDXID': id, 'name': name, 'versionInfo': version, 'downloadLocation': 'NOASSERTION', 'externalRefs': []map[string]string{{ 'referenceCategory': 'PACKAGE_MANAGER', 'referenceType': 'purl', 'referenceLocator': purl, }}, }}, } b, _ := json.Marshal(doc) return b } func generateDoc(t *testing.T, fsys apkfs.FullFS, pkgs ...*apk.InstalledPackage) *Document { t.Helper() opts := testOpts(fsys) opts.Packages = pkgs out := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), 'sbom.spdx.json') if err := New().Generate(context.Background(), opts, out); err != nil { t.Fatalf('Generate: %v', err) } b, err := os.ReadFile(out) if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) } var doc Document if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &doc); err != nil { t.Fatal(err) } return &doc } func packageVersions(doc *Document) map[string]string { m := map[string]string{} for _, p := range doc.Packages { m[p.Name] = p.Version } return m } func TestEmbeddedSBOMIdentity(t *testing.T) { t.Run('mismatched SBOM substitutes a fake package', func(t *testing.T) { fsys := apkfs.NewMemFS() _ = fsys.MkdirAll('var/lib/db/sbom', 0o755) _ = fsys.WriteFile('var/lib/db/sbom/evil-helper-1.0.0-r0.spdx.json', embeddedSBOM('SPDXRef-Package-openssl-9.9.9-r0', 'openssl', '9.9.9-r0', 'pkg:apk/wolfi/openssl@9.9.9-r0?arch=x86_64'), 0o644) got := packageVersions(generateDoc(t, fsys, installedPkg('evil-helper', '1.0.0-r0', 'evil-helper'))) t.Logf('packages: %v', got) if _, ok := got['evil-helper']; ok { t.Errorf('evil-helper present') } if got['openssl'] != '9.9.9-r0' { t.Errorf('fake openssl absent') } }) t.Run('package without SBOM is silently dropped', func(t *testing.T) { fsys := apkfs.NewMemFS() _ = fsys.MkdirAll('var/lib/db/sbom', 0o755) got := packageVersions(generateDoc(t, fsys, installedPkg('no-sbom', '1.0.0-r0', 'no-sbom'))) t.Logf('packages: %v', got) if _, ok := got['no-sbom']; ok { t.Errorf('no-sbom present') } }) t.Run('malformed SBOM is silently dropped', func(t *testing.T) { fsys := apkfs.NewMemFS() _ = fsys.MkdirAll('var/lib/db/sbom', 0o755) _ = fsys.WriteFile('var/lib/db/sbom/broken-1.0.0-r0.spdx.json', []byte('{not json'), 0o644) got := packageVersions(generateDoc(t, fsys, installedPkg('broken', '1.0.0-r0', 'broken'))) t.Logf('packages: %v', got) if _, ok := got['broken']; ok { t.Errorf('broken present') } }) t.Run('earlier SBOM shadows a real package by SPDX ID', func(t *testing.T) { fsys := apkfs.NewMemFS() _ = fsys.MkdirAll('var/lib/db/sbom', 0o755) _ = fsys.WriteFile('var/lib/db/sbom/aaa-1.0.0-r0.spdx.json', embeddedSBOM('SPDXRef-Package-openssl-3.0.1-r0', 'openssl', '3.5.0-r0', 'pkg:apk/wolfi/openssl@3.5.0-r0?arch=x86_64'), 0o644) _ = fsys.WriteFile('var/lib/db/sbom/openssl-3.0.1-r0.spdx.json', embeddedSBOM('SPDXRef-Package-openssl-3.0.1-r0', 'openssl', '3.0.1-r0', 'pkg:apk/wolfi/openssl@3.0.1-r0?arch=x86_64'), 0o644) got := packageVersions(generateDoc(t, fsys, installedPkg('aaa', '1.0.0-r0', 'aaa'), installedPkg('openssl', '3.0.1-r0', 'openssl'))) t.Logf('packages: %v', got) if got['openssl'] != '3.5.0-r0' { t.Errorf('shadowing did not occur: openssl=%q', got['openssl']) } }) t.Run('name-only fallback lets another package author the entry', func(t *testing.T) { fsys := apkfs.NewMemFS() _ = fsys.MkdirAll('var/lib/db/sbom', 0o755) // busybox ships no SBOM of its own (e.g. a non-melange apk); another // package ships var/lib/db/sbom/busybox.spdx.json, which the linter accepts. _ = fsys.WriteFile('var/lib/db/sbom/busybox.spdx.json', embeddedSBOM('SPDXRef-Package-busybox-9.9.9-r0', 'busybox', '9.9.9-r0', 'pkg:apk/wolfi/busybox@9.9.9-r0?arch=x86_64'), 0o644) got := packageVersions(generateDoc(t, fsys, installedPkg('busybox', '1.36.1-r0', 'busybox'))) t.Logf('packages: %v', got) if got['busybox'] != '9.9.9-r0' { t.Errorf('fallback not taken: busybox=%q', got['busybox']) } }) } ``` ### Patches None released yet. The fix, in `pkg/sbom/generator/spdx`: 1. reads an embedded document only from a path the installed database lists among the package's own files, so a document another package installs is ignored, 2. requires every described record, and every record carrying an apk PURL, to name the installed package at its version, with or without the `-rN` epoch, so a package's own apk entry cataloged as a reachable record stays valid, 3. rejects a reachable record that uses an installed package's canonical SPDX ID, 4. fails the build when a package's own document does not parse, describes nothing, or describes an element that is not a package, 5. describes a package that ships no document from its installed-database entry and logs a warning, and 6. fails the build when two records share an SPDX ID but differ in name, version, external references, or checksums, rather than keeping the first. Records that differ only in metadata, such as the license, are kept once, and apko logs a warning. It also returns an error, rather than dereferencing a nil `FileInfo`, when inspecting an SBOM path fails for a reason other than the path not existing. ### Limits of the fix The fix binds each embedded document to the package that ships it: a document cannot describe another package, claim another installed package's SPDX ID, or carry another package's apk PURL. It does not make the document's other records trustworthy. A package's document still attests to its own dependencies and upstream sources, so a crafted apk can add records naming components it does not contain, provided they carry no apk PURL and no installed package's SPDX ID. An SBOM consumer can trust the apk records, but should treat the non-apk records as claims made by the package that ships them. A crafted apk can also reuse another document's SPDX ID with a different name, version, reference, or checksum to make the build fail. apko refuses to build the image rather than record false content. ### Workarounds * Build only from repositories whose publishers you trust and whose packages melange builds. * Compare the SBOM's package list with `/lib/apk/db/installed` in the image, or scan the image filesystem rather than the SBOM.

CVE-2024-36127.description: apko is an apk-based OCI image builder. apko exposures HTTP basic auth credentials from repository and keyring URLs in log output. This vulnerability is fixed in v0.14.5.

CVE-2026-105768.title: apko allows users to build and publish OCI container images built ...
CVE-2026-105768.description: apko allows users to build and publish OCI container images built from apk packages. From version 0.2.0 to before version 1.4.5, UserEntry.Parse and GroupEntry.Parse in pkg/passwd read the UID and GID fields of /etc/passwd and /etc/group entries with strconv.Atoi and convert them to uint32 without a range check. On 64-bit platforms an out-of-range value such as 4294967296 (2^32) is truncated to 0, and negative values wrap. Because apko parses the passwd and group entries supplied by the packages it installs and writes them back into the image, an attacker who controls a package installed into the image can ship an entry that appears to declare an unprivileged UID or GID but is written into the built image as UID 0 or GID 0 (root). The truncated UID is also used when resolving the image's run-as user. This issue has been fixed in version 1.4.5.

CVE-2026-42575.title: apko allows users to build and publish OCI container images built ...
CVE-2026-42575.description: apko allows users to build and publish OCI container images built from apk packages. Prior to version 1.2.7, apko verifies the signature on APKINDEX.tar.gz but never compares individually downloaded .apk packages against the checksum recorded in the signed index. The checksum is parsed and available via ChecksumString(), and the downloaded package control hash is computed, but the two values are never compared in getPackageImpl(). Mismatched packages are silently accepted. An attacker who can substitute download responses (compromised mirror, HTTP repository, poisoned CDN cache) can install arbitrary packages into built images. This issue has been patched in version 1.2.7.

CVE-2026-42576.description: apko allows users to build and publish OCI container images built from apk packages. Prior to version 1.2.7, DiscoverKeys in pkg/apk/apk/implementation.go unconditionally type-asserts JWKS keys as *rsa.PublicKey without checking the key type. If a repository JWKS endpoint returns a non-RSA key (e.g. EC), the unchecked assertion panics and crashes apko. This affects any workflow that initializes the APK database and fetches repository keys. This issue has been patched in version 1.2.7.

A crafted package can embed a newline in that data, terminating the current record and forging an entire additional package record. The installed database is the source for SBOM generation (`pkg/build/sbom.go`, `pkg/build/build.go`), so forged records propagate into apko's SPDX output. The significant consequence is **concealment** rather than addition: an attacker who can place a package in a repository the build trusts can install a vulnerable component while forging a record that reports a different name or version, causing downstream vulnerability scanners that consume the SBOM to miss the real component. ### Scope This advisory covers one mechanism: **control characters — a newline in particular — carried in package data into installed-database records.** It does not claim to close every route by which a package can misrepresent itself in the SBOM. The fix is the byte-level validation described under Patches, not a general guarantee that recorded package identity matches the package installed. ### Affected data paths Three distinct families of attacker-influenced data reach these records. All were unvalidated. **1. Package metadata from `.PKGINFO` (no filesystem interaction required).** `PackageToInstalled` (`pkg/apk/apk/package.go`) renders `P:`, `V:`, `T:`, `L:`, `o:`, `m:`, `U:`, `D:`, `p:`, `r:` and `c:` lines directly from parsed `.PKGINFO` values. apk-tools reads `.PKGINFO` as a plain `key = value` line splitter with no quoting, and so can neither produce nor observe a multi-line value. apko parses it with `gopkg.in/ini.v1` (`pkg/apk/types/package.go`), which honours backquoted and triple-quoted multi-line values by default. A triple-quoted `pkgdesc` therefore carries an embedded newline straight into the database. This is the most accessible variant — it needs nothing more than a crafted `pkgdesc` field, and apko explicitly prefers `.PKGINFO` over APKINDEX as the more complete source (`pkg/apk/apk/implementation.go`), so the permissive parser is the one that reaches the database. **2. Archive entry names.** `AddInstalledPackage` (`pkg/apk/apk/installed.go`) writes `F:` and `R:` lines from `tar.Header.Name`. No control-character validation existed anywhere in `pkg/apk`; `sanitizeArchivePath` guards only path traversal. Both install paths were affected — `installAPKFiles` and the `lazilyInstallAPKFiles` fastpath that `installPackage` selects whenever the backing filesystem implements `WriteHeaderer`, which is the normal apko configuration. Control-section entry names reached `usr/lib/apk/db/scripts.tar` in the produced image by the same route, via `updateScriptsTar`. **3. PAX checksum records.** The `Z:` line forwards an `APK-TOOLS.checksum.SHA1` PAX record unchanged when it already carries a `Q1` prefix. `installAPKFiles` recomputes that record for regular files, but the symlink and hardlink branches pass the supplied value through untouched. No filesystem-level access or unusual configuration is required. ### Patches Fixed by validating at each source and again at the sink: - `.PKGINFO` values containing a newline or carriage return are rejected at parse time in `types.ParsePackageInfo`, restoring agreement with apk-tools about what the format permits with respect to line breaks. Neither can reach it from a database read. An empty name is accepted there because it is the representation of the top-level directory. - Every rendered database line is checked for an embedded newline or carriage return immediately before the record is written, which covers the `Z:` passthrough and any field that acquires such a value in future. The record is now built entirely before the database file is opened, so a rejection cannot leave a created-but-empty database behind. - `ParseInstalled` no longer returns a short package list with a nil error when a record line exceeds the scanner's buffer. An over-long line previously stopped the scan silently, so a single such line erased every record after it from the parsed result and therefore from the SBOM — the same concealment impact, reached without a control character. The bound is raised to accommodate legitimately long dependency lines, and exceeding it is now an error. - `ParseInstalled` no longer discards `sanitizeArchivePath`'s error, which had converted a path traversal in an `R:` value into a file header with an empty name. - An install that fails part-way leaves entries written and claimed in the in-memory ownership map, which later packages' records are filtered against. The Go port compares unsigned bytes and carries regression tests pinning that legitimate UTF-8 names remain acceptable. Upstream applies `contains_control_character()` to the archive entry name only — `src/database.c`, one call site, on `ae->name`. apko matches that scope deliberately: link targets are not validated, because they never become an `F:` or `R:` value and so cannot forge a record, and rejecting them would refuse packages that `apk add` installs without complaint. The metadata variant has no upstream analogue, because apk-tools' line-based `.PKGINFO` reader cannot represent it. ### Related Before [#2328](https://github.com/chainguard-dev/apko/pull/2328), an entry name embedding a single-character line also reached an out-of-range slice panic in `ParseInstalled`, making that denial of service reachable from a package rather than only from a corrupt base image. That specific path is closed by #2328. GHSA-45cw-mp53-rrv6.title: apk-embedded SPDX documents can hide, impersonate, and displace packages in apko image SBOMs
GHSA-45cw-mp53-rrv6.description: ### Impact apko builds the package portion of an image's SPDX SBOM entirely from SPDX documents that the installed apks ship under `/var/lib/db/sbom`. It never checks that a document describes the package that shipped it, and it omits a package without error when that package's document is missing or fails to parse. A crafted apk can therefore: * remove itself from the image SBOM, * appear under another name and version, with a well-formed PURL, and * replace the record of a genuine package, for example reporting a patched version of a vulnerable library. Tools that trust the SBOM act on the false data: SBOM-driven vulnerability scanners, policy engines that evaluate SBOM attestations, and license reports. apko generates the SBOM before the image is signed, so attestations built from it verify cleanly. The image's `/lib/apk/db/installed` still lists the true package set, so scanners that inspect the image filesystem are unaffected. Images built from repositories whose packages carry no embedded SBOM, such as Alpine, receive an SBOM with no apk packages at all, with no attacker involved. ### Affected data paths All in `pkg/sbom/generator/spdx/spdx.go`, the only SBOM generator in apko: 1. [`locateApkSBOM`](https://github.com/chainguard-dev/apko/blob/e3915900849d95b35f1f5b7c7401922505332152/pkg/sbom/generator/spdx/spdx.go#L185-L206) chooses a document by file name alone, trying `<name>-<version>.spdx.json`, then the version without its `-rN` suffix, then `<name>.spdx.json`. It never checks that the installed package owns the file. 2. [`ProcessInternalApkSBOM`](https://github.com/chainguard-dev/apko/blob/e3915900849d95b35f1f5b7c7401922505332152/pkg/sbom/generator/spdx/spdx.go#L214-L224) returns `nil` when no document matches or the document fails to parse. 3. [`ProcessInternalApkSBOM` and `copySBOMElements`](https://github.com/chainguard-dev/apko/blob/e3915900849d95b35f1f5b7c7401922505332152/pkg/sbom/generator/spdx/spdx.go#L226-L331) copy every package the document describes. Nothing compares name, version, SPDX ID, or PURL against the installed package. 4. [`Generate`](https://github.com/chainguard-dev/apko/blob/e3915900849d95b35f1f5b7c7401922505332152/pkg/sbom/generator/spdx/spdx.go#L163-L173) deduplicates packages by SPDX ID and keeps the first. melange assigns predictable IDs, `SPDXRef-Package-<name>-<version>` ([melange `pkg/sbom/package.go:147`](https://github.com/chainguard-dev/melange/blob/d062cf25ce373bf8045d79b9897878ab207d8d36/pkg/sbom/package.go#L147)), so a document processed earlier can displace a genuine record. 5. [Lines 156-160](https://github.com/chainguard-dev/apko/blob/e3915900849d95b35f1f5b7c7401922505332152/pkg/sbom/generator/spdx/spdx.go#L156-L160) are the only place apk packages enter the SBOM. apko never falls back to the installed database. ### Scope * **Packages built by melange cannot replace their own document.** melange runs the build pipelines ([`pkg/build/build.go:671`](https://github.com/chainguard-dev/melange/blob/d062cf25ce373bf8045d79b9897878ab207d8d36/pkg/build/build.go#L671)) and then writes `<name>-<version>.spdx.json`, truncating any existing file ([`build.go:847`](https://github.com/chainguard-dev/melange/blob/d062cf25ce373bf8045d79b9897878ab207d8d36/pkg/build/build.go#L847), [`pkg/build/sbom/spdx/spdx.go:257`](https://github.com/chainguard-dev/melange/blob/d062cf25ce373bf8045d79b9897878ab207d8d36/pkg/build/sbom/spdx/spdx.go#L257)). * **A melange pipeline can add further `*.spdx.json` files** to `var/lib/db/sbom`. melange's `sbom` linter flags only files without that suffix ([`pkg/linter/linters/sbom.go:30`](https://github.com/chainguard-dev/melange/blob/d062cf25ce373bf8045d79b9897878ab207d8d36/pkg/linter/linters/sbom.go#L30)) and warns by default ([`pkg/linter/linter.go:87-90`](https://github.com/chainguard-dev/melange/blob/d062cf25ce373bf8045d79b9897878ab207d8d36/pkg/linter/linter.go#L87-L90)). apko uses such a file for any co-installed package that lacks a correctly named document of its own. * **No package can overwrite another origin's document.** apko refuses to install two packages from different origins that ship the same path with different content ([`pkg/apk/apk/install.go:141-149`](https://github.com/chainguard-dev/apko/blob/e3915900849d95b35f1f5b7c7401922505332152/pkg/apk/apk/install.go#L141-L149)). ### Attack prerequisites The attacker must place a crafted apk in the resolved package set of a build, for example by publishing it to a repository the build trusts. No access to the build host is required. ### Affected versions All releases through 1.4.5. Unchecked ingestion of embedded documents ships in v0.7.0 and later. Keep-first deduplication by SPDX ID, which enables displacement of genuine records, ships in v0.19.3 and later (#1366). ### Proof of concept A table-driven test against `SPDX.Generate` on an in-memory filesystem, confirmed at `e3915900` and `739e7ce`. `Generate` returns `nil` in every case. | Scenario | Installed | Embedded SBOM | apk entries in image SBOM | | -- | -- | -- | -- | | Substitution | `evil-helper 1.0.0-r0` | `evil-helper-1.0.0-r0.spdx.json` describes `openssl 9.9.9-r0`, `pkg:apk/wolfi/openssl@9.9.9-r0` | `openssl 9.9.9-r0` only | | Missing SBOM | `no-sbom 1.0.0-r0` | none | none | | Malformed SBOM | `broken 1.0.0-r0` | `{not json` | none | | Displacement | `aaa 1.0.0-r0`, `openssl 3.0.1-r0` | `aaa`'s document reuses `SPDXRef-Package-openssl-3.0.1-r0` with version `3.5.0-r0` | `openssl 3.5.0-r0`; the genuine `3.0.1-r0` record is dropped | | Name-only fallback | `busybox 1.36.1-r0`, no document of its own | added `busybox.spdx.json` says `9.9.9-r0` | `busybox 9.9.9-r0` | Save as `pkg/sbom/generator/spdx/embedded_sbom_identity_test.go` and run `go test ./pkg/sbom/generator/spdx/ -run TestEmbeddedSBOMIdentity -v`. Each subtest passes while the defect exists. ```go package spdx import ( 'context' 'encoding/json' 'os' 'path/filepath' 'testing' 'chainguard.dev/apko/pkg/apk/apk' apkfs 'chainguard.dev/apko/pkg/apk/fs' ) func installedPkg(name, version, origin string) *apk.InstalledPackage { return &apk.InstalledPackage{Package: apk.Package{Name: name, Version: version, Origin: origin, Arch: 'x86_64'}} } func embeddedSBOM(id, name, version, purl string) []byte { doc := map[string]any{ 'SPDXID': 'SPDXRef-DOCUMENT', 'spdxVersion': 'SPDX-2.3', 'documentDescribes': []string{id}, 'packages': []map[string]any{{ 'SPDXID': id, 'name': name, 'versionInfo': version, 'downloadLocation': 'NOASSERTION', 'externalRefs': []map[string]string{{ 'referenceCategory': 'PACKAGE_MANAGER', 'referenceType': 'purl', 'referenceLocator': purl, }}, }}, } b, _ := json.Marshal(doc) return b } func generateDoc(t *testing.T, fsys apkfs.FullFS, pkgs ...*apk.InstalledPackage) *Document { t.Helper() opts := testOpts(fsys) opts.Packages = pkgs out := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), 'sbom.spdx.json') if err := New().Generate(context.Background(), opts, out); err != nil { t.Fatalf('Generate: %v', err) } b, err := os.ReadFile(out) if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) } var doc Document if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &doc); err != nil { t.Fatal(err) } return &doc } func packageVersions(doc *Document) map[string]string { m := map[string]string{} for _, p := range doc.Packages { m[p.Name] = p.Version } return m } func TestEmbeddedSBOMIdentity(t *testing.T) { t.Run('mismatched SBOM substitutes a fake package', func(t *testing.T) { fsys := apkfs.NewMemFS() _ = fsys.MkdirAll('var/lib/db/sbom', 0o755) _ = fsys.WriteFile('var/lib/db/sbom/evil-helper-1.0.0-r0.spdx.json', embeddedSBOM('SPDXRef-Package-openssl-9.9.9-r0', 'openssl', '9.9.9-r0', 'pkg:apk/wolfi/openssl@9.9.9-r0?arch=x86_64'), 0o644) got := packageVersions(generateDoc(t, fsys, installedPkg('evil-helper', '1.0.0-r0', 'evil-helper'))) t.Logf('packages: %v', got) if _, ok := got['evil-helper']; ok { t.Errorf('evil-helper present') } if got['openssl'] != '9.9.9-r0' { t.Errorf('fake openssl absent') } }) t.Run('package without SBOM is silently dropped', func(t *testing.T) { fsys := apkfs.NewMemFS() _ = fsys.MkdirAll('var/lib/db/sbom', 0o755) got := packageVersions(generateDoc(t, fsys, installedPkg('no-sbom', '1.0.0-r0', 'no-sbom'))) t.Logf('packages: %v', got) if _, ok := got['no-sbom']; ok { t.Errorf('no-sbom present') } }) t.Run('malformed SBOM is silently dropped', func(t *testing.T) { fsys := apkfs.NewMemFS() _ = fsys.MkdirAll('var/lib/db/sbom', 0o755) _ = fsys.WriteFile('var/lib/db/sbom/broken-1.0.0-r0.spdx.json', []byte('{not json'), 0o644) got := packageVersions(generateDoc(t, fsys, installedPkg('broken', '1.0.0-r0', 'broken'))) t.Logf('packages: %v', got) if _, ok := got['broken']; ok { t.Errorf('broken present') } }) t.Run('earlier SBOM shadows a real package by SPDX ID', func(t *testing.T) { fsys := apkfs.NewMemFS() _ = fsys.MkdirAll('var/lib/db/sbom', 0o755) _ = fsys.WriteFile('var/lib/db/sbom/aaa-1.0.0-r0.spdx.json', embeddedSBOM('SPDXRef-Package-openssl-3.0.1-r0', 'openssl', '3.5.0-r0', 'pkg:apk/wolfi/openssl@3.5.0-r0?arch=x86_64'), 0o644) _ = fsys.WriteFile('var/lib/db/sbom/openssl-3.0.1-r0.spdx.json', embeddedSBOM('SPDXRef-Package-openssl-3.0.1-r0', 'openssl', '3.0.1-r0', 'pkg:apk/wolfi/openssl@3.0.1-r0?arch=x86_64'), 0o644) got := packageVersions(generateDoc(t, fsys, installedPkg('aaa', '1.0.0-r0', 'aaa'), installedPkg('openssl', '3.0.1-r0', 'openssl'))) t.Logf('packages: %v', got) if got['openssl'] != '3.5.0-r0' { t.Errorf('shadowing did not occur: openssl=%q', got['openssl']) } }) t.Run('name-only fallback lets another package author the entry', func(t *testing.T) { fsys := apkfs.NewMemFS() _ = fsys.MkdirAll('var/lib/db/sbom', 0o755) // busybox ships no SBOM of its own (e.g. a non-melange apk); another // package ships var/lib/db/sbom/busybox.spdx.json, which the linter accepts. _ = fsys.WriteFile('var/lib/db/sbom/busybox.spdx.json', embeddedSBOM('SPDXRef-Package-busybox-9.9.9-r0', 'busybox', '9.9.9-r0', 'pkg:apk/wolfi/busybox@9.9.9-r0?arch=x86_64'), 0o644) got := packageVersions(generateDoc(t, fsys, installedPkg('busybox', '1.36.1-r0', 'busybox'))) t.Logf('packages: %v', got) if got['busybox'] != '9.9.9-r0' { t.Errorf('fallback not taken: busybox=%q', got['busybox']) } }) } ``` ### Patches None released yet. The fix, in `pkg/sbom/generator/spdx`: 1. reads an embedded document only from a path the installed database lists among the package's own files, so a document another package installs is ignored, 2. requires every described record, and every record carrying an apk PURL, to name the installed package at its version, with or without the `-rN` epoch, so a package's own apk entry cataloged as a reachable record stays valid, 3. rejects a reachable record that uses an installed package's canonical SPDX ID, 4. fails the build when a package's own document does not parse, describes nothing, or describes an element that is not a package, 5. describes a package that ships no document from its installed-database entry and logs a warning, and 6. fails the build when two records share an SPDX ID but differ in name, version, external references, or checksums, rather than keeping the first. Records that differ only in metadata, such as the license, are kept once, and apko logs a warning. It also returns an error, rather than dereferencing a nil `FileInfo`, when inspecting an SBOM path fails for a reason other than the path not existing. ### Limits of the fix The fix binds each embedded document to the package that ships it: a document cannot describe another package, claim another installed package's SPDX ID, or carry another package's apk PURL. It does not make the document's other records trustworthy. A package's document still attests to its own dependencies and upstream sources, so a crafted apk can add records naming components it does not contain, provided they carry no apk PURL and no installed package's SPDX ID. An SBOM consumer can trust the apk records, but should treat the non-apk records as claims made by the package that ships them. A crafted apk can also reuse another document's SPDX ID with a different name, version, reference, or checksum to make the build fail. apko refuses to build the image rather than record false content. ### Workarounds * Build only from repositories whose publishers you trust and whose packages melange builds. * Compare the SBOM's package list with `/lib/apk/db/installed` in the image, or scan the image filesystem rather than the SBOM.
